overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, all three positive segments are detected with no false alarms.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Two of three hidden instances are strict true positives. The substitution mechanism is detected and localized but receives the wrong label, representativeness heuristic.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: All three hidden mechanisms are correctly localized and matched at high_and_moderate, with perfect mechanism-first precision and recall before candidate inclusion.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate is a useful abstention because it remains separate from identified findings, but counting candidates as detections adds one false alarm on the neutral final-sign-off segment.
main_failure_modes: Near-neighbor taxonomy error: substitution bias was labeled representativeness heuristic.
Candidate inclusion creates a false alarm on the intentionally neutral final decision.
main_strengths: All three hidden decision episodes were localized correctly.
All three hidden mechanisms were captured, including the substitution mechanism despite the label error.
Automation bias was identified with direct evidence, and illusory correlation was an approved equivalent label for the hidden correlation-bias construct.
The ambiguous final decision was not promoted to an identified bias.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment detection and mechanism-first identification at the recommended threshold, but strict label performance is reduced by one taxonomy error. Candidate-level scoring reveals a modest false-alarm cost without improving recall.
